name: Physical Intelligence
description: Builds general-purpose robot foundation models (pi-0, pi-0.5) and now sells them through an API that lets other companies fine-tune and run inference on their own hardware. name: Skild AI

name: Generalist

name: Field AI

name: Flexion Robotics

name: Gemini Robotics

name: Qwen

name: RLWRLD

name: World Labs

name: Odyssey

name: AMI

name: Embo

name: Veeda AI

name: Vsim

name: RoboLab

description: A dynamic mobile manipulator combining a legged base with a working arm, so it can both traverse rough industrial sites and do work when it arrives.

name: RIVR
description: Wheeled-legged delivery robots that climb steps to the door, closing the last few metres that sidewalk robots cannot. Spun out of ETH's Swiss-Mile.

name: Bubble Robotics
description: BubbleDock stations and BubbleBots that stay at sea six months doing offshore inspection. Docks stay on station for six months so inspection is continuous rather than one mission at a time, sold as a service.

name: Sevensense Robotics
description: Visual SLAM that lets AMRs navigate from cameras alone, with no reflectors or magnetic tape to install; acquired by ABB.

name: Voliro
description: Thrust-vectoring drones that touch structures to perform non-destructive testing. Its drones physically touch structures to take ultrasonic readings, replacing rope access and scaffolding on tanks, flare stacks and bridges.

name: Embotech
description: Optimisation-based motion planning, now applied commercially to driverless vehicle movement in ports, yards and finished-vehicle logistics. The planning software is the product, which is why it is here rather than in a vertical.

name: Nautica Technologies
description: Swarms of underwater robots that clean and inspect ship hulls to stop biofouling. Biofouling costs ships fuel and forces toxic antifouling paint; its OceanMind system runs the swarm without GPS or a diver.

name: Flink Robotics
description: ETH Zurich spin-off whose software makes a robot plug-and-play for material handling, so a site can add one without an integration project.

name: Disney Research
description: Disney's research lab, behind expressive character robots and the simulation work underneath them - robotics judged on how it reads to an audience rather than cycle time.

name: Tethys Robotics
description: Underwater robots for inspection and search in fast-flowing, zero-visibility water. Works in fast-flowing, zero-visibility water where divers cannot safely go, for police search and infrastructure inspection.

name: Auterion
description: Open operating system for drones and autonomous systems, widely used in defense. Now the de facto standard software layer for Western defence drones, after Ukraine made interoperability a procurement requirement.

name: April Robotics
description: Automates the finest, highest-precision work in manufacturing, where tolerances are tighter than conventional automation handles.

name: microagi
description: Zurich lab building embodied AI models and the research behind them; early-stage and not yet shipping a product.

name: Loki Robotics
description: Cleaning robots for commercial restrooms and kitchens - jobs with high turnover and chronic staffing problems. Zurich-based, $1.6M pre-seed led by byFounders.

name: Hexagon Robotics
description: Zurich robotics company from the Lukas Ziegler map.
notes: UNVERIFIED - on the Ziegler Zurich map but no company found

name: Wingtra
description: VTOL fixed-wing survey drones that take off vertically then fly like a plane, mapping large sites in one flight rather than many battery swaps.

name: Ascento
description: Wheeled-legged robots that patrol industrial sites and perimeters outdoors in weather, handling kerbs and stairs that wheeled security robots cannot. Sold as a security service rather than as hardware.

name: Amazon Robotics
description: The largest deployed robot fleet on earth, inside Amazon's own fulfillment network. Over a million units inside Amazon's own network, which makes it the only organisation operating robots at true industrial scale.

name: Teradyne Robotics
description: Parent of Universal Robots and MiR, making it the largest collaborative robot and mobile robot group by installed base.

name: Symbotic
description: High-density automated case handling built out across Walmart's distribution network, which has committed to running a large share of its volume through automated facilities. The largest listed pure-play in warehouse robotics.

name: Oxipital AI
description: Machine vision for food and consumer goods handling, where products vary in shape; formerly Soft Robotics.

name: iRobot
description: Roomba proved consumers would buy a robot at all, and defined home robotics for two decades. Now under pressure from cheaper rivals, and taken private in 2026.

name: Berkshire Grey
description: Robotic picking and sortation for retail and parcel, deployed with Walmart, FedEx and Target. Taken private in 2023 after a SPAC that did not hold.

name: Vecna Robotics
description: Autonomous forklifts and tuggers with human-in-the-loop remote support, so a trained operator resolves exceptions across many trucks instead of riding one.

name: 6 River Systems
description: Chuck, the collaborative picking cart that walks warehouse associates through orders; built by Shopify, sold on to Ocado.

name: Vicarious Surgical
description: A surgical robot with camera and arms inserted through a single incision, aimed at ventral hernia repair. Publicly listed, and the main reason this map has a surgical category at all.

name: Boost Robotics
description: Mobile manipulators as remote hands for data center inspection and maintenance (YC). Positions robots as 'remote hands' so technicians are not dispatched for every fix, and patrols the hall the rest of the time (YC).

name: RightHand Robotics
description: AI piece-picking for each-order fulfillment, deployed across European and US retail. Piece-picking individual items for each-order fulfilment, deployed across European and US retail and pharmacy distribution.

name: RISE Robotics
description: Belt-driven electric actuator built to replace hydraulic cylinders on heavy equipment. Replacing hydraulic cylinders removes the fluid, the leaks and much of the energy loss from heavy equipment.

name: Toyota Research Institute
description: Toyota's research arm, which pioneered large behavior models for robots - teaching manipulation from demonstration rather than programming. Walden Robotics spun out of it.

name: Piaggio Fast Forward
description: gita, a two-wheeled cargo robot that follows a person at walking pace carrying up to 20kg. Piaggio's bet on personal mobility rather than fleet logistics, which is why it sits apart from the sidewalk delivery companies.

name: GreenSight
description: Autonomous drones and analytics for turf, golf courses and agriculture, selling the agronomic insight rather than the aircraft.

name: Sereact
description: One brain for any robot: perception and control models for pick-and-place at scale. Stuttgart-based, selling perception and control models for pick-and-place into European logistics rather than building its own robot.

name: Pickle Robot
description: Robots that unload floor-loaded trucks and shipping containers, the job warehouses struggle hardest to staff. Deployed across major US distribution centre operators.

name: Acumino
description: Wearable device that teaches robots tasks in one shot, without a data-collection program. Teaches a task in one shot from a wearable device, so a customer does not fund a data-collection programme before seeing value.

name: Analog Devices
description: Precision sensing, motion control and interface silicon underneath industrial robots - the parts between the sensor and the processor.

name: Urbx
description: TowerBots climb storage grids up to 125 feet to retrieve totes, so urban grocery fulfilment fits into 1,800 square feet instead of a warehouse.

name: Realtime Robotics
description: Motion planning in microseconds, which lets several arms share one workcell without colliding or being choreographed by hand.

name: Code Metal
description: Verifiable code translation and compilation for edge and embedded robotics targets. Translates and verifies code for edge and embedded targets, the step where robotics software most often breaks between prototype and product.

name: Sea Machines Robotics
description: Autonomous control and remote command for commercial workboats, letting one mariner supervise several vessels rather than crewing each.

name: Humanoid
description: London humanoid developer scaling production in partnership with Bosch, which gives it manufacturing capacity most startups lack.

name: Tennibot
description: Autonomous ball collection and AI ball machines for tennis, pickleball and padel. A rare consumer robotics company with a working unit economic story, selling into clubs as well as households.

name: MathWorks
description: MATLAB and Simulink, the modelling and control toolchain a large share of robotics is still designed and verified in.

name: General Robotics
description: GRID platform of modular AI skills for perception, reasoning and control; ex-Scaled Foundations.

name: Isaac Sim
description: NVIDIA's Omniverse-based simulator, and the default target for generating synthetic data and running reinforcement learning at scale. Listed separately from NVIDIA because robotics teams adopt it as its own tool.

name: Gazebo
description: The long-running open-source simulator maintained alongside ROS; the default in academic robotics.

name: Drake
description: Toyota Research's physics and planning toolbox, built for contact-rich manipulation and control.

name: Freedom Robotics
description: Hardware-agnostic fleet monitoring, remote access and diagnostics, priced per robot per month for teams too small to build their own.

name: Transitive Robotics
description: An open framework for building your own web-based fleet tools; its transAct dashboard ships teleoperation, config and health out of the box.

name: SVT Robotics
description: SOFTBOT connects robots to WMS and ERP systems as reusable microservices, cutting an integration from months to weeks.

name: SYNAOS
description: Intralogistics platform running mixed AGV and AMR fleets from 50+ manufacturers over the VDA 5050 interface.

name: NAiSE
description: Vendor-neutral orchestration with indoor tracking, running mixed AGV and AMR fleets across more than two dozen brands.

name: BlueBotics
description: ANT navigation and fleet software licensed to vehicle makers, so an AGV builder does not have to write its own autonomy.

name: Meili Robots
description: Brand-agnostic fleet management, so AMRs from different vendors share one traffic controller instead of fighting over aisles.

name: KINEXON
description: Industrial operating system with centralised AMR and AGV orchestration, built around real-time location of everything on the floor.

name: MOV.AI
description: A ROS-based robotics engine for building, deploying and operating autonomous mobile robots, aimed at integrators rather than labs.

name: Open-RMF
description: Open-source layer that coordinates multiple robot fleets and the building around them - lifts, doors, traffic between vendors.

name: Ottopia
description: Teleoperation software where a remote human and the vehicle's own AI share control during an intervention. BMW selected it as a preferred teleoperation technology and Motional uses it for robotaxi support.

name: DriveU.auto
description: Autonomous retrofit kits for container-port terminal tractors, built on its teleop connectivity stack.

name: Kineo Finance
description: Venture leasing and working capital for as-a-service hardware; did the Kiwibot sale-leaseback.

name: Cenotian
description: Capital plus engineering for robotics deployments: funds design through commissioning, billed monthly or per use.

name: Miso Robotics
description: Flippy, the autonomous fry station, sold as a service into quick-service kitchens. Deployed with White Castle and Jack in the Box, in the one kitchen station with the worst injury and turnover numbers.

name: Anduril
description: Builds autonomous aircraft, maritime craft, counter-UAS and munitions, tied together by Lattice, its command software. The defining company of the defence-tech wave and the one most others are measured against.

name: Shield AI
description: Hivemind is autonomy software that flies aircraft without GPS or a pilot, shipped on its own V-BAT and now the X-BAT fighter. Sells both the aircraft and the autonomy stack to other platforms.

name: Saronic
description: Builds autonomous surface vessels at shipyard scale for the US Navy, having bought its own yard to do it.

name: Forterra
description: AutoDrive ground autonomy for military logistics, with 105 Lancer vehicles built and delivered in under six months. $238M Series C.

name: Overland AI
description: OverDrive is off-road ground autonomy for uncrewed military vehicles, built for terrain with no lanes, no map and no GPS. Sold as a stack that goes onto existing platforms rather than as a vehicle.

name: Neros Technologies
description: US-made FPV attack drones produced at volume, built to break dependence on Chinese airframes and components.

name: HavocAI
description: Low-cost autonomous surface vessels built for maritime swarming, where numbers matter more than the capability of any one hull.

name: Vatn Systems
description: Autonomous underwater vehicles designed for mass manufacture, so navies can field them in numbers rather than as bespoke assets.

name: Blue Water Autonomy
description: Full-size unmanned ships designed without crew from the keel up, rather than retrofitting a hull built for people.

name: ARX Robotics
description: European unmanned ground vehicles and a retrofit autonomy kit for legacy fleets. Its retrofit kit converts legacy military vehicles to uncrewed operation, which matters more in Europe than building new platforms.

name: Allen Control Systems
description: Bullfrog, a robotic gun turret that shoots drones out of the sky with small arms - a cheaper counter-UAS answer than a missile.

name: True Anomaly
description: Autonomous spacecraft for orbital security and space domain awareness, built to manoeuvre and inspect other satellites rather than just observe from the ground.

name: Varda
description: Autonomous orbital capsules that manufacture pharmaceuticals in microgravity and return them to Earth - robotics applied to a process that cannot happen on the ground.

name: Greypoint Industries
description: Maps the electromagnetic spectrum from a drone swarm, so a unit can see and locate every emitter on a battlefield.

name: Ornadyne
description: Flapping-wing UAVs that look and fly like real birds, built to be near-silent and visually unremarkable for reconnaissance.

name: Edgerun
description: Military exoskeletons that add strength and endurance, starting with a hip system worn over existing kit.

name: Applied Intuition
description: Autonomy and simulation stack for automotive, defense, trucking, construction and mining. Valued around $15B, selling the autonomy and simulation stack to carmakers and defence primes rather than operating vehicles itself.

name: Wayve
description: End-to-end learned driving that adapts to any vehicle without HD maps, sold to carmakers rather than operated as a fleet. Backed by SoftBank, Nvidia and Microsoft.

name: VulcanForms
description: Digital metal additive manufacturing run as its own production infrastructure - it sells parts rather than printers, at volumes conventional additive cannot reach.

name: Bright Machines
description: Software-defined assembly cells for electronics and data centre hardware, where product changes faster than a hard-tooled line can be rebuilt.

name: Auris Health
description: The Monarch platform drives a flexible robotic endoscope into the lung or kidney, reaching targets a surgeon's hand cannot steer to. Acquired by Johnson & Johnson for $3.4B, which set the price anchor for surgical robotics.

name: Capstan Medical
description: Robotic catheter delivery of replacement heart valves, so a valve can be placed without open-chest surgery.

name: Build AI
description: Data hyperscaler for physical AI, scaling core research bets by orders of magnitude. Sells the data pipeline rather than the model, betting that data volume is the binding constraint on physical AI.

name: Cortex AI
description: Collects large-scale real-world robot and human data for embodied AI, selling the dataset rather than the model trained on it (YC F25).

name: DeepReach
description: A distributed network of vetted data partners wearing stereo capture devices, recording how people actually do physical work.

name: Preload
description: Gives robots a nervous system: everyday video paired with synchronised force and motion capture, built as a training-data stack.

name: Robocurve
description: A public benefit corporation running independent real-world evaluations of physical AI, so claims about robot performance can be checked.

name: Runtime
description: Evaluation layer that tests robot policies across thousands of simulated environments (YC).

name: Enact
description: Builds physical test environments for benchmarking and improving robotics models, where simulation stops being representative.

name: Moving Atoms
description: A video-pretrained physics model that simulates what a robot action will do, aimed at generating training data without a physics engine (YC).

name: Aktoria Robotics
description: Low-latency teleoperation software plus a 24/7 robot operations centre of trained operators across the US, Mexico and India. Customers get remote intervention without staffing their own control room, and the sessions become training data.

name: Ember Robotics
description: Helps robotics engineering teams trace hardware failures, track releases and investigate incidents across a deployed fleet.

name: Autumn Labs
description: A manufacturing intelligence platform that monitors industrial robots and the processes around them, surfacing faults before they stop the line.

name: Polymath Robotics
description: Drop-in autonomy for industrial vehicles - tractors, loaders, yard trucks - exposed as an API so a vehicle maker can add self-driving without an autonomy team (YC S22).

name: Agency Tool Company
description: Over-the-air software updates and fleet management built for robots rather than phones, so a fleet in the field can be patched safely.

name: Dreamscale Labs
description: Real-time cloud inference for robots, so a team can run frontier models without putting an expensive GPU on every machine.

name: Hebbian Robotics
description: Open-source foundational infrastructure for physical AI, aimed at the plumbing every robotics team currently rebuilds.

name: Synapse Semiconductor
description: A vision sensor that runs neural network filters on the pixels themselves, cutting the data and power cost of perception before anything reaches a processor (YC).

name: Proception
description: Dexterous humanoid hands sold to other robot makers, aimed at the gap between a two-finger gripper and a human hand (YC W25).

name: Silica
description: Force-sensing actuators sold at a price point that lets small teams build dexterous robots without custom drive trains.

name: Open Actuation
description: Designs and manufactures custom robotic actuators and drone motors in Los Angeles, for builders who need something off-catalogue.

name: Mass Magnetics
description: Rare-earth magnets made in America from recycled feedstock, aimed at the single most China-dependent input in a robot joint.

name: Piggy Robotics
description: Building humanoid robots for household chores, competing on price rather than capability. Competing on price rather than capability, which is the opposite bet to most of the humanoid field (YC F25).

name: Nori
description: The NORI A3, an affordable bimanual robot for home and office, made in the US and sold at a price closer to an appliance than a humanoid.

name: Charge Robotics
description: A field factory that assembles solar rows automatically and places them, aimed at the labour shortage limiting utility-scale solar build rates. MIT founders, YC S21, with its first commercial system shipped.
lead_investor: Founders Fund, Energy Impact Partners and Lux

name: Libra Robotics
description: AI that adapts robots quickly to infrastructure work like solar farm construction (YC). Targets infrastructure work like solar construction, where tasks repeat but sites never do (YC).

name: BotBuilt
description: Robotic house framing installed inside existing lumber yards, so the automation goes where the material already is (YC W21).

name: Pave Robotics
description: Autonomous asphalt crack sealing for highways, municipalities and parking lots - a repetitive roadside job that is dangerous to staff and easy to defer.

name: Flywheel AI
description: Autonomy for excavators, with a command centre so one operator supervises several machines rather than sitting in a cab (YC S25).

name: Teleo
description: Retrofit kits that make existing heavy construction equipment supervised-autonomous. Retrofits existing heavy equipment rather than selling new machines, so a contractor keeps the fleet they already financed.

name: Shepherd Robotics
description: General-purpose robots for data centres and electrical equipment manufacturing, including switchgear assembly (YC).

name: Proprio Robotics
description: Builds robots aimed at small businesses, starting with data centre buildout, maintenance and decommissioning work (YC).

name: Manifold
description: Autonomous picking, loading and palletizing in warehouses, priced per pick (YC). Charging per pick rather than per robot puts the performance risk on Manifold rather than the warehouse (YC).

name: AutoPallet Robotics
description: Warehouse automation rebuilt around pallets rather than totes, moving loads that case-handling systems cannot.

name: Theseus Robotics
description: Humanoids that restock supermarket shelves and rotate stock overnight, then pick grocery orders by day.

name: Odin Robotics
description: Puts robot arms into small and mid-sized factories to do repetitive manual work - machine tending, packing - alongside equipment that is already there (YC).

name: Shiraz AI
description: Deploys factory robots that learn a new manufacturing task from one human demonstration, so a line can be changed over without reprogramming.

name: Mbodi AI
description: Software that lets industrial robots learn tasks the way a person would, rather than being programmed path by path.

name: Advanced Metal Research
description: Open-source, AI-native industrial robots and machines for metal fabrication, including robotic welding cells with vision-based seam tracking.

name: Industrial Next
description: Vision-driven autonomous manufacturing cells, out of Tesla's manufacturing team. Founded by Tesla manufacturing veterans, applying the vision-first approach that worked on their own lines.

name: Atomic Industries
description: AI tool-and-die maker automating the most skilled trade in manufacturing (YC W21). Tool and die is among the most skilled and least automated trades in manufacturing, with a retiring workforce and no replacements (YC W21).

name: Salem Robotics
description: Turns robots into autonomous inspection and compliance workers, starting in nuclear facilities where human entry is costly and limited.

name: Rodeo Robotics
description: A robotic maintenance system that keeps vehicle fleets ready for work, starting with routine servicing at depots. Technicians work alongside it, and their hand tools are instrumented so the work becomes training data.

name: Neuromorphic
description: Robots that work autonomously inside existing wet labs, running the repetitive bench work that paces biology experiments (YC).

name: Primordiant
description: Embodied scientific intelligence: general-purpose robotic experimentalists that plan, run and interpret physical experiments.

name: Rhem Labs
description: A tabletop robot an older adult can talk to - conversation, games and medication reminders - aimed at independent living rather than clinical care.

name: Deploy
description: Deployment infrastructure for getting generalist robots running inside a business (YC). Sells the deployment infrastructure rather than the robot, betting that getting generalist robots into a business is the hard part (YC).

name: RoboShare
description: Rental marketplace matching robot owners with customers; handles booking, pricing and service delivery.

name: UBTech
description: Walker S industrial humanoid, shipping into Chinese auto plants for inspection and sorting work. HK-listed, and among the first humanoids in paid factory deployment.

name: Fourier Intelligence
description: GR-series humanoids out of Shanghai, grown from a rehabilitation robotics business - which gave it force-control experience most humanoid startups lack.

name: Robot Era
description: Tsinghua spin-out building humanoids and dexterous hands, among the better-funded of the Chinese humanoid cohort.

name: XPeng Robotics
description: The IRON humanoid, funded and manufactured off XPeng's electric vehicle base - which gives it a supply chain most humanoid startups lack.

name: Rainbow Robotics
description: Korea's largest listed robot company, making cobots and bipeds; Samsung took a controlling stake in 2025.

name: Kawasaki Robotics
description: One of the big five industrial arm makers, strong in spot welding and heavy handling, plus the duAro dual-arm cobot.

name: DENSO Robotics
description: Compact SCARA and six-axis arms under 20kg payload, aimed at electronics and medical assembly where cycle time and footprint matter more than reach. Part of DENSO, the automotive supplier.

name: Mitsubishi Electric
description: MELFA industrial arms sold alongside the PLCs, drives and controls around them - a single-vendor factory stack.

name: Omron
description: Sensing, control, safety and cobots in one catalogue, plus the mobile robot line acquired from Adept - a full factory-floor stack.

name: Doosan Robotics
description: Collaborative arms with joint torque sensing as standard, which makes force-controlled tasks possible out of the box. KOSPI-listed since 2023.

name: Estun
description: China's largest domestic industrial robot maker, vertically integrated to the servo. Vertically integrated down to its own servo motors, which is how it competes with the big four on price inside China.

name: Siasun
description: State-backed Chinese robot maker spun out of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, with the broadest domestic industrial robot range.

name: JAKA
description: Collaborative arms sold on price into the Asian and European mid-market, part of the Chinese cobot wave undercutting Universal Robots.

name: MiR
description: The default autonomous mobile robot for moving material around a factory floor, sold through a large integrator network. Part of Teradyne alongside Universal Robots.

name: Harmonic Drive Systems
description: Invented the strain wave gear, which is still the reducer most precision robot joints use. Every Chinese harmonic competitor is priced relative to it, so it sets the floor for the whole joint supply chain.

name: Nabtesco
description: Cycloidal reducers carrying most of the world's industrial robot joints - a near-duopoly with Harmonic Drive on the single most critical robot component.

name: Laifual
description: Harmonic reducers and integrated actuator modules at 40-60% of Japanese pricing. One of the Chinese reducer makers undercutting Harmonic Drive on price, and a reason humanoid bills of materials keep falling.

name: Tuopu Group
description: Auto supplier turned robot actuator maker; named in Tesla Optimus supply chain. Spending RMB 5bn on a dedicated robot electric-drive base, which is how fast the Chinese supply chain is repositioning.

name: ZHAOWEI
description: Micro drive systems and China's first high-degree-of-freedom dexterous hand, supplying motors into other makers' hands.

name: Robotiq
description: The default gripper and force-torque sensor for collaborative arms, and the reason most cobot pilots can start without custom tooling.

name: SCHUNK
description: The broadest gripper and workholding catalogue in the industry, covering nearly any part a machine needs to grip or clamp. The default answer when a cell needs standard tooling.

name: OnRobot
description: One-stop end-of-arm tooling - grippers, sensors, tool changers - built so a cobot can be switched between jobs in minutes.

name: Hesai
description: Lidar at automotive volume, now pushing into robotics; Nasdaq-listed and the largest lidar maker by units shipped.

name: RoboSense
description: Lidar and perception systems at automotive volume, now pushed into robotics; HK-listed and one of the two Chinese lidar majors.

name: Keyence
description: Machine vision, sensors and measurement sold direct with no distributors, which is why its margins are the envy of the sector.

name: Cognex
description: The machine vision incumbent - In-Sight cameras and barcode reading - deployed across most automated factories and warehouses.

name: SICK AG
description: Safety laser scanners and industrial sensing that most guarded robot cells legally depend on.

name: Keli Sensing
description: Six-axis force-torque sensors in volume production, rare outside Japan and Germany and a bottleneck for Chinese dexterous hands.

name: Paxini
description: Multimodal tactile skin and fingertips that give dexterous hands a sense of touch, sold to humanoid and hand makers.

name: Geek+
description: The largest AMR fleet by units shipped, deployed across global third-party logistics providers and retailers. The Chinese company that made goods-to-person automation affordable.

name: Hai Robotics
description: Case-handling robots that climb racking to retrieve totes at height, turning existing warehouse shelving into dense automated storage.

name: Acieta
description: North American robot integrator with more than 10,000 systems deployed and over $1B of installed automation. The kind of firm that performs most industrial robot deployments, and the layer the neo-integrator thesis argues is ripe for disruption.

name: JR Automation
description: Custom automated manufacturing and distribution systems; 27 facilities worldwide. A Hitachi company with over 2,000 staff, and one of the few integrators that can take a global programme.

name: Bastian Solutions
description: Warehouse automation integrator inside the largest systems integrator group in logistics. Part of Toyota's logistics group, now the largest systems integrator in warehouse automation by revenue.

name: Dematic
description: Intralogistics systems integrator; designs, builds and services automated warehouses. KION-owned, and one of the handful of integrators capable of building and servicing a fully automated distribution centre.

name: Vanderlande
description: Baggage, parcel and warehouse systems at airport and national scale - the company behind the baggage handling in much of Europe. Toyota-owned, and one of the largest integrators by revenue.

name: Swisslog
description: Designs, builds and services automated warehouses and hospital logistics systems; the KUKA-owned integrator in intralogistics.

name: Honeywell Intelligrated
description: Full-systems warehouse integrator with its own controls and software, so a customer buys the conveyor, the robots and the orchestration from one party.

name: Applied Manufacturing Technologies
description: Independent automation engineering and integration services since 1989, working for end users and OEMs without being tied to one robot brand.

name: ATS Corporation
description: Global automation systems integrator for life sciences, electric vehicles and consumer goods, building the production line rather than selling the robots in it.

name: Robo Reliance
description: Third-party field service for commercial robots, OEM-agnostic, with independent technicians recruited and trained market by market. Lets a robot maker offer nationwide support without building the organisation.

name: BOW Robotics
description: Industrial robot repair and maintenance across FANUC, ABB, KUKA and Motoman fleets. Services other makers' arms nationwide, so a plant with a mixed fleet has one number to call.

name: SafeWorld
description: Simulation that tests robot safety before deployment, aimed at the certification gap between a working policy and a system that can legally operate near people.

name: TUV Rheinland
description: Functional safety certification against ISO 10218 and ISO 13482, plus CE marking. One of the notified bodies a robot has to pass through before it can be sold into Europe, which makes it gatekeeper as much as vendor.

name: TUV SUD
description: Machinery safety audits, gap analysis and CE marking readiness, including for the EU Machinery Regulation that becomes mandatory in 2027.

name: SGS
description: CE notified body testing robotic products for electrical, mechanical and EMC safety. A CE notified body, so its sign-off is what lets a robotic product enter the European market.

name: Automation Rangers
description: Independent robot and machine risk assessments and CE marking consultancy, working with TUV Rheinland, TUV SUD and UL on certification.

name: Pacific Blue Engineering
description: Machine safety consultancy: risk assessment, guarding and safety circuit validation. Does risk assessment, guarding design and safety circuit validation with TUV-certified engineers - the work that makes a cell legal to run.

name: Inxpect
description: 3D radar safety sensing that sees through dust, steam and spark - conditions where light curtains and safety lidar fail - so a cell can stay guarded in a real foundry.

name: Rockwell Automation
description: Safety controls, guarding and PLCs, plus risk assessments delivered by TUV-certified consultants - the incumbent most factory safety systems are built on.

name: Dexmate
description: Vega, a folding wheeled humanoid with a 7ft reach, from $89,999; backed by LG CNS and NEC.

name: Coco Robotics
description: Runs about 1,300 electric sidewalk robots across Los Angeles, Miami, Chicago and Helsinki for Subway, Wingstop and Jack in the Box. Its OpenAI deal runs both ways: Coco gets model access, OpenAI gets real-world road data.
lead_investor: SNR, with Sam Altman as an angel

name: Project Prometheus
description: Bezos and Vik Bajaj's stealth lab building what it calls an 'artificial general engineer': AI that designs and manufactures complex physical systems, from jet engines to drug compounds. Closer to AI-native CAD than to robot control, but it is the largest-funded physical-world AI effort in existence.

name: Eccentric Machines
description: AI-designed actuators sold together with the motion software that drives them, so the control and the mechanism are co-designed.

name: Modal Motors
description: High-torque motors made in America without rare-earth magnets, addressing both the supply risk and the cost of the magnet itself.

name: Endiatx
description: PillBot is a swallowable robot that streams live video from inside the stomach, replacing sedated endoscopy for routine examination.

name: Purple Rhombus
description: Uncrewed aircraft designed for rapid scale-up and immediate combat use, prioritising production rate over per-unit capability.

name: Alloy Robotics
description: AI agents that read a robot fleet's logs and diagnose why something failed, aimed at the engineering time lost to debugging deployed robots. Founded in Sydney in 2025 and expanding into the US.

name: Viam
description: A single platform covering robot configuration, control, data capture and fleet management, so a team does not assemble five tools to ship one robot. Founded by Eliot Horowitz after MongoDB, and aimed at companies that want to avoid building their own stack.

name: Nuro
description: Pivoted from building its own delivery pods to licensing the Nuro Driver to carmakers and fleet operators, so it now sells autonomy rather than vehicles.

name: Kodiak AI
description: Driverless trucks running commercially in the Permian Basin; public since 2025. Its trucks haul for energy customers off public highways first, where the regulatory burden is lighter. Public via SPAC in 2025.

name: Numurus
description: NEPI, an edge AI platform that makes sensors and payloads interoperable, so an integrator can swap hardware without rewriting the stack.

name: THK
description: Invented the linear motion guide; the rails and ballscrews most machines slide on. Its rails and ballscrews are inside most machine tools and many robots, a component so standard it is usually invisible.

name: WITTENSTEIN
description: Low-backlash servo gearboxes and complete drive systems for precision robotics, where positioning accuracy under load is the specification that matters.

name: Nidec Drive Technology
description: Cycloidal and planetary reducers at volume, the main alternative to Nabtesco and part of Nidec's push into robot joints.

name: ADVANCED Motion Controls
description: Servo drives and motion controllers for robots and autonomous vehicles - the electronics that turn a control signal into motor torque.

name: Cone Drive
description: Precision gearboxes and slew drives, including alternatives to harmonic reducers for applications where backlash matters less than torque.

name: Performance Motion Devices
description: Motion control ICs and modules sitting between the controller and the motor, sold to machine builders designing their own drives.

name: ElectroCraft
description: Fractional-horsepower motors and gearmotors for mobile robots and medical devices. Supplies the small motors inside mobile robots and medical devices, below the size range the big industrial names bother with.

name: Motus Labs
description: Gearboxes using a meshless design aimed at higher torque density than harmonic drives. Its meshless gearbox design targets higher torque density than harmonic drives, aimed at the humanoid joint market.

name: Bishop-Wisecarver
description: Guided motion systems, linear actuators and track rollers - the mechanical components a robot moves along rather than the robot itself.

name: Doodle Labs
description: Mesh Rider radios: resilient private networking for drones, robots and field teams. Mesh radios that keep working when cellular does not, which is why they turn up on defence drones and field robots.

name: WiBotic
description: Wireless charging and power optimisation for drone, AMR and underwater fleets, so robots recharge without a docking connector to misalign or corrode.

name: VARTA
description: Lithium cells and battery packs for mobile robots and cordless equipment, the power source under most AMRs and service robots.

name: RoboDock
description: Automated charging for electric and autonomous vehicle fleets, so a fleet can run without a human plugging anything in (YC W2026).

name: RGo Robotics
description: Perception Engine giving AMRs human-like spatial understanding from cameras alone. Gives AMRs spatial understanding from cameras alone, so an integrator does not install reflectors or tape to make navigation work.

name: NVIDIA Jetson
description: Thor and Orin modules are the default on-robot compute, and NVIDIA builds GR00T to run on them. This is where most companies' models physically execute once a robot is on a customer site.

name: Hailo
description: Edge AI accelerators running transformer models at a few watts, for battery-powered robots.

name: Qualcomm Robotics
description: Snapdragon-based robotics platforms (RB series) where low power and connectivity matter most.

name: Ambarella
description: Low-power vision SoCs doing perception on-device in cameras, drones and robots. Competes with Hailo and NVIDIA at the low-power end, where a camera or drone cannot carry a Jetson.

name: Axelera AI
description: Edge inference silicon aimed at datacenter-class throughput inside an embedded power budget.

name: Apex.AI
description: Apex.Grace is a ROS 2-compatible SDK certified to ISO 26262 ASIL D, which is what lets autonomy software ship in a production vehicle rather than a pilot. Supplies middleware to tier-one suppliers including HL Klemove's ADAS controllers.

name: ZettaScale
description: Zenoh, the pub/sub protocol replacing DDS where robots need to talk across the network edge.

name: eProsima
description: Fast DDS, the middleware underneath ROS 2 communication, plus the commercial support that production users need.

name: Adamo
description: Managed teleoperation as a service: the software plus the operators, for autonomous vehicles, humanoids and industrial arms. Founded 2025 by James Naylor and Sam Considine, aimed at teams that need remote intervention without staffing their own control room.

name: Sanctuary AI
description: Builds Phoenix, a humanoid with hydraulic hands and unusually rich tactile sensing, controlled by its Carbon software. Teleoperation is explicit in the design: human operators feel what the robot feels, which both supervises the work and generates the training data.

name: Reflex Robotics
description: A wheeled humanoid aimed at reliable repetitive work rather than demos, with remote operators covering what autonomy misses.

name: Vay
description: Teledriving: a human drives the car remotely from a station with real controls, no autonomy claimed. Runs a commercial mobility service in Las Vegas and licenses the stack to others, including Kodiak.

name: Fernride
description: Teleoperation-first ground autonomy for yard trucks and container handling, where a remote operator supervises several vehicles and autonomy takes over the routine legs.

name: Human Archive
description: Records how people do physical work and turns it into training data for embodied models, betting that human demonstration is the scarce input (YC W2026).

name: Cogito Tech
description: Managed training-data operations, including teleoperation capture and annotation of multimodal robot data.
